title: React Module 05 Applied Check
description: Apply state and event handling concepts to immutable updates, batching, stale closures, event behavior, and shared state scenarios.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What is the likely result of calling `setCount(count + 1); setCount(count + 1);` in one click handler?

options.text: The count may increase by 1 because both updates used the same snapshot
React throws because two setters are illegal

questions.explanation: State values are snapshots during a render. Use functional updates when queuing multiple updates based on previous state.

questions.prompt: Which replacement reliably increments twice in one handler?
questions.explanation: Each functional updater receives the latest queued value.

questions.prompt: Which are immutable ways to update array state? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Spread, filter, and map create new arrays. Pushing mutates the existing array.

questions.prompt: A form submit reloads the page unexpectedly. What is the usual fix in the submit handler?
questions.explanation: Preventing the default form submission lets React handle the submit without a page reload.

questions.prompt: Calling a state setter directly while rendering can create a render loop.
questions.explanation: Render should be pure. Unconditional state updates during render cause React to render again repeatedly.

questions.prompt: A child button should notify its parent with an item id. Which pattern is best?
questions.explanation: Wrap the callback so it runs on click, not during render.

questions.prompt: Which choices help avoid stale closures? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Use functional state updates when next state depends on previous state
Put changing values in the right dependency list for effects
Assume a timeout callback always sees the newest state
Use refs intentionally for mutable latest values when appropriate

questions.explanation: Functional updates, correct dependencies, and carefully used refs address common stale value issues.

questions.prompt: Two controls must stay synchronized with one selected tab value. What is the most reliable design?

options.text: One parent owns `selectedTab` and passes it plus change callbacks down
Each child stores unrelated local selected tab state
Use a regular variable outside React
Read the DOM to find the active tab

questions.explanation: A single source of truth keeps siblings synchronized.
